justification: Liability fix to the live public /climate-risk tool + card + marketing page. The result card and page presented a composite 1-100 climate 'risk score' with a verdict band and traffic-light (green->red) colour coding — both explicitly prohibited by the org's own climate-risk legal assessment (ce-climate-risk-score-legal-assessment lines 77, 81), and a smoke test showed the verdict is misleading cross-location (Byron Bay 'Very High' with 9 heat days vs Penrith 'Moderate' with 87). Standard tier: user-facing copy/UI only, no logic/data-flow/DB change, but legal-sensitive — the risk is a residual verdict/traffic-light cue slipping through, covered by the sweep + break-it below.

pre_impl.existing_data: The card/page consumed the existing /pipeline/climate-risk response (score, band, hazards, narclim_summary). The brief already retired the composite score for a 'Climate Disclosure Profile' (intelligence_brief.py:807) — this brings the standalone tool in line. No API/response shape change; the API still returns score/band, the UI simply stops rendering them as a verdict.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The composite score/band is dominated by coastal/flood weighting, so it inverts on heat (coastal town out-scores a far hotter western suburb) — confirmed live across 6 NSW climate zones. So the fix removes the composite headline entirely rather than recolouring it, and leads with the factual per-hazard exposure + NARCliM projection metrics (which are sound and correctly differentiated).
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new components; edits to the existing card/tool/page. Present/Not-present badge style reused from the rewritten card in the page's sample mockup for consistency.

functions: N/A — frontend TSX copy/presentation change; no Python functions, no new logic.
values: N/A — no data reads changed; the card renders the same API fields, minus the composite score/band verdict.
queries: N/A — no database access; no API contract change.

break_it.scenario: A residual traffic-light (green/amber/red) cue implies a safety/danger verdict
break_it.what_happens: would breach the legal posture (line 81). Swept: the composite score/band headline, the green->red band ladder, the per-hazard X/20 colour chips, and the red/amber projection numbers were all removed/neutralised to gray on both the card and the page's sample mockup
break_it.how: grep confirms no user-facing '/100', 'Very High', 'risk score', 'composite score', or hazard-verdict green/red remains (hazard-TYPE and data-TYPE icon colours are not verdicts and are kept)
break_it.repro: grep -inE 'risk score|composite score|/ 100|Very High|score out of' frontend-nextjs/components/tools/ClimateRiskResultCard.tsx frontend-nextjs/app/climate-risk/page.tsx | grep -v '//'

break_it.scenario: Banned liability language (safe/suitable/insurable/at-risk) in the climate copy
break_it.what_happens: would breach the language audit + legal posture; climate copy is the highest-risk text
break_it.how: 'Suitable for insurance assessments' removed; explicit 'not a risk rating / prediction / statement about insurability, safety or value' framing added to the card header and disclaimer

break_it.scenario: The page's hardcoded sample mockup contradicts the real (rewritten) card
break_it.what_happens: users would be shown an example output they will not actually receive
break_it.how: the sample header and per-hazard chips were converted to the same neutral exposure-count + Present/Not-present style the live card now renders
break_it.repro: visual: /climate-risk sample section matches ClimateRiskResultCard output

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes — load /climate-risk, run a real address, confirm the result card leads with hazard exposure + NARCliM projection metrics (each sourced), shows NO composite score/band verdict and NO green/red risk colouring, and the disclaimer states it is not a risk rating or financial advice. Follow-up (not this PR): the page's hardcoded sample mockup could be regenerated from a live response for full fidelity.
